data.title: Weak Active Directory Password Policy
data.summary:
The domain password policy permitted short passwords and did not prevent the use
of predictable or previously breached values, allowing a significant proportion of
account passwords to be recovered.
data.description:
The Active Directory password policy enforced a minimum length below current
recognised guidance and applied no restriction on commonly used or organisationally
predictable values. Complexity requirements alone do not prevent passwords that
follow predictable patterns such as a season or company name combined with a year
and a symbol.

Analysis of recovered password hashes showed widespread use of such patterns,
including among accounts holding elevated privileges.
data.impact:
An attacker could recover valid credentials through password spraying or offline
cracking of captured hashes. Because the affected accounts include privileged
users, this provides a route from no access at all to administrative control of
the domain, without requiring the exploitation of any software vulnerability.
data.recommendation:
1. Increase the minimum password length to at least 14 characters for standard
   accounts and 25 characters for privileged and service accounts.

2. Deploy a password filter or Azure AD Password Protection to block common,
   breached, and organisationally predictable passwords at the point of change.

3. Encourage the use of passphrases and deploy an approved password manager so
   that longer values remain practical for users.

4. Configure an account lockout threshold that mitigates online password guessing
   while accounting for the risk of denial of service, and monitor for spraying
   patterns across many accounts.

5. Conduct a periodic domain password audit against a breached-password corpus and
   force resets for any account whose password is recovered.
